key_insight: OmegaUse-OfficeVal shows that current LLM agents can complete office-suite workflows cheaply, but their deliverable quality still falls short of human workers on long-horizon tasks.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps engineers compare agent cost versus human labor and assess value-weighted performance for office automation systems.
method: Built a 100-task benchmark from practitioner office-suite requests using a privacy-preserving adaptation process.
Annotated each task with two economic signals: estimated human labor time and a task price proxy.
Created code-based verifiers from fine-grained rubrics for more stable and reproducible evaluation.
evidence_signal: The benchmark tasks average 2.32 hours of human labor each, and evaluations compare several frontier LLMs against a human baseline using both quality and economic measures.
watch_item: Task-level economic proxies may not transfer cleanly across organizations or changing market conditions, so benchmark results should be interpreted as context-dependent.
paper_title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
